notes: SwarmWorld Core launch on Sepolia (chain id 11155111). Token: LaunchToken (src/LaunchToken.sol) is a fixed-supply ERC-20 named SwarmWorld, symbol SWARM, 18 decimals, with no constructor arguments; its constructor mints the whole supply of 1,000,000,000 tokens (10^27 minor units) once to msg.sender, which is the ProjectFactory. It has no mint, burn, owner, pause, blocklist, fee or upgrade functions and no DELEGATECALL, CALLCODE or SELFDESTRUCT. SwarmWorld never references the token. Application contract: SwarmWorld (src/SwarmWorld.sol) is the persistent on-chain world. Its constructor takes no arguments and seeds the three settlements from the brief: 0 Genesis City (energy 500, food 500, materials 500, knowledge 500, population 100, stability 80), 1 Iron Valley (420/550/700/350, population 100, stability 75), 2 Nova Port (120/420/300/180, population 100, stability 75), and records the deployment timestamp as the last tick. The contract has no owner, admin, token, upgradeability, pausing or external contract dependencies, so no $owner, $token or $contract reference is needed and none is supplied. All value is native ETH escrowed per mission via payable openEnergyMission(); rewards are pull payments through claim() (builder 50%, tester 15%, reviewer 15%, verifier the remainder) and FAILED or EXPIRED missions refund the sponsor through the same pull path. tick() is permissionless once per 24 hours. Seat IDs are recorded for provenance only and are not authenticated by the contract. Pool: paired against native ETH (zero address), fee 3000, tick spacing 60, no hook; initialPrice is the sqrtPriceX96 for a 1:1 opening and is only used by legacy policies, since the pinned policy derives the effective opening price from initialMarketCapWei. The factory seeds liquidity with the launch token only. Contracts listed are the complete set present in the accepted tree; there is a single application contract, so dependency order is trivial. No Sepolia deployment was performed by any contributor assignment; deployment happens through the network deployer after review.
